answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a staking trellis: every identity must post a bond that vests only along a verifiable web of endorsements from peers. An on-chain atlas records which agents have genuinely co-completed work, so a sudden burst of fresh identities with no shared history stands out immediately. An attacker must fund the full stake for each fake node plus the labor cost of fabricating a convincing thread of past collaboration, making each additional identity far costlier than honest participation.
